preconditions.expression: all(2 <= n <= 20000 and 1 <= m <= 10000 for n, m in [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[:1]])
preconditions.description: Input must contain exactly one line with integers n (number of cities) and m (number of citizens), where 2 ≤ n ≤ 20000 and 1 ≤ m ≤ 10000.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == 2 + (n - 1) + m and all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:1 + (n - 1)]) and all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1 + (n - 1):])
preconditions.description: Input must contain exactly n-1 lines for roads (each with two distinct city numbers) followed by m lines for citizens (each with two distinct city numbers).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= v <= n and 1 <= u <= n and v != u for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:1 + (n - 1)] for v, u in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: Each road connects two distinct cities numbered from 1 to n.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n and x != y for line in stdin.splitlines()[1 + (n - 1):] for x, y in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: Each citizen's home and work cities are distinct and numbered from 1 to n.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().splitlines()[0].isdigit() and (k := int(stdout.strip().splitlines()[0])) >= 1 and k <= n
postconditions.description: The first line of output is a single integer k (1 ≤ k ≤ n), representing the minimum number of puppies needed.

Output consists of exactly three lines: the first line is k, the second line starts with q followed by q distinct citizen indices, and the third line starts with e followed by e distinct road indices.

postconditions.expression: (q, *citizens) := map(int, stdout.strip().splitlines()[1].split()) and all(1 <= a <= m for a in citizens) and len(set(citizens)) == q
postconditions.description: The second line starts with q (number of puppies given to citizens), followed by q distinct citizen indices (1 ≤ ai ≤ m).

postconditions.expression: (e, *guardians) := map(int, stdout.strip().splitlines()[2].split()) and all(1 <= b <= n - 1 for b in guardians) and len(set(guardians)) == e
postconditions.description: The third line starts with e (number of puppies given to guardians), followed by e distinct road indices (1 ≤ bi ≤ n - 1).
The sum of puppies given to citizens (q) and guardians (e) equals the total number of puppies k.

postconditions.expression: (roads := [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:1 + (n - 1)]]) and (citizen_paths := [get_shortest_path(roads, int(x) - 1, int(y) - 1) for x, y in [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1 + (n - 1):]]]) and all(len(path) >= 1 for path in citizen_paths)
postconditions.description: For each citizen, compute the shortest path (as a list of road indices) from their home city to their work city using BFS or similar. The path is 0-indexed for internal use.

postconditions.expression: (puppies_to_citizens := set(citizens)) and (puppies_to_guardians := set(guardians)) and all(any(citizen in puppies_to_citizens for citizen in range(1, m + 1) if all(road in puppies_to_guardians for road in citizen_paths[citizen - 1])) or citizen in puppies_to_citizens for citizen in range(1, m + 1))
postconditions.description: For every citizen, either the citizen is given a puppy (citizen in puppies_to_citizens) or all guardians along their path are given puppies (all roads in their path are in puppies_to_guardians).

postconditions.expression: not any(citizen in puppies_to_citizens and all(road in puppies_to_guardians for road in citizen_paths[citizen - 1]) for citizen in range(1, m + 1))
postconditions.description: No citizen is redundantly given a puppy when all guardians along their path are already given puppies.
